experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim and snorkeling among the rock formations.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local wineries in the Lagoa DOC wine region, the heart of Algarve winemaking. Tour the vineyards, learn about indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco, and enjoy guided tastings of crisp whites, rosés, and robust reds paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most photographed sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos, arched rock formations, and secret beaches along the dramatic Algarve coastline, combining adventure with breathtaking natural beauty.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Local Seafood Dinner
experiences.description: Visit the windswept Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of Europe, for a dramatic Atlantic sunset. Afterward, dine at a traditional tasca in Sagres village, savoring freshly grilled cataplana (seafood stew), percebes (barnacles), and local Algarve wine in an authentic fishing village atmosphere.
experiences.location: Sagres & Cabo de São Vicente, Vila do Bispo

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Oyster Tasting
experiences.description: Take a guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park of tidal channels, barrier islands, and wildlife. Stop at a local oyster farm to taste freshly harvested oysters paired with chilled Algarve white wine, and explore the pristine barrier island beaches accessible only by boat.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. €5-7, ~1.5 hours). Check in to Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24h petrol station near the bus terminal or a kebab shop near Lagos center (~€3-5)

day_by_day.notes: Keep your arrival simple. The bus from Faro to Lagos is the cheapest option. Book tickets in advance at rede-expressos.pt. The hostel is a short walk or cheap taxi (~€5) from Lagos bus station. Get a good night's rest.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, enjoy the hostel's common area. Walk to the Lagos Old Town and explore the historic center: visit Igreja de Santo António (free exterior), the old city walls, and Praça Gil Eanes. Pick up a local SIM card at a nearby phone shop for cheap data (~€10-15).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 15 minutes south to Meia Praia or take the short ferry (€1.50 each way) across the estuary to Meia Praia beach. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing on this long, calm sandy beach — one of the most accessible from Lagos. The water in mid-September is still warm (~22°C).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll back into Lagos old town for the evening. Walk along the marina and watch the sunset over the harbor. Explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril for budget dining options.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or any local pastelaria near the hostel — coffee + pastel de nata (~€2)
meals.lunch: Grab a prego (steak sandwich) or bifana from a local snack bar near the beach (~€3-4)
meals.dinner: O Camilo or a local tasca on Rua 25 de Abril — prato do dia (dish of the day) with wine (~€8-10)

day_by_day.notes: September is shoulder season in Algarve — beaches are less crowded and prices drop slightly. Sunscreen is essential as UV levels remain high. The hostel may offer free maps of Lagos.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Praia Dona Ana, one of Lagos's most iconic beaches with dramatic golden cliffs. It's a 20-minute walk south from the hostel. Arrive early to secure a good spot. Explore the cliff-top walking path toward Ponta da Piedade for stunning rock formation views — completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the coastal walk to Ponta da Piedade lighthouse and grottos viewpoint. For a budget sea cave experience, rent a kayak from the beach (~€15/hour) or join a shared boat tour of the grottos (~€15-20 per person). Return to the hostel to rest during the hottest part of the day.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Lagos wine bar scene. Visit Adega do Cantor or a local wine shop offering Algarve regional wines by the glass. Try a glass of Algarve red or white wine (~€2-3/glass). Join the hostel's social hour if available.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast if included, or a local café — toast, juice, coffee (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local Mercado Municipal (fresh bread, cheese, fruit, ~€4-5) and eat at the clifftop
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina — grilled sardines or cataplana for one (~€9-12)

day_by_day.notes: The walk from Dona Ana to Ponta da Piedade is about 2km along cliff paths. Wear sturdy sandals or trainers. Bring water. The grottos kayak rental is best in the morning when seas are calmer.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus (Eva Bus, ~€3) or rent a bicycle from the hostel (~€10/day) to Praia da Luz, a charming village beach 6km west of Lagos. Arrive early and enjoy the calm, sheltered bay. Explore the small village with its whitewashed church and seafront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue west by bus or bike to Burgau, a tiny fishing village with a beautiful small beach. Walk the coastal trail between Luz and Burgau (approx. 4km, 1 hour) for spectacular cliff scenery. Swim at Praia de Burgau.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Visit the Mercado de Lagos (if open late) or browse the artisan shops on Rua da Barroca. Enjoy the Friday evening atmosphere in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Padaria (bakery) near the hostel — fresh bread roll with butter and coffee (~€2)
meals.lunch: Snack bar in Praia da Luz — grilled fish sandwich or salad (~€6-8)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso in Lagos old town — traditional Portuguese petiscos (tapas-style small plates, ~€8-10)

day_by_day.notes: Renting a bicycle is a great budget option for exploring the coast. The coastal walk between Luz and Burgau is part of the Via Algarviana trail. Bring a windbreaker as sea breezes can be strong in the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres — take the Eva Bus from Lagos bus station (~€4.50, 1 hour). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry), a 15th-century fortress at the southwestern tip of Europe. Explore the windswept promontory and the famous wind compass (rosa dos ventos).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Cabo de São Vicente (Cape St. Vincent), the most southwesterly point of mainland Europe. The views are breathtaking. Visit the lighthouse (small entry fee ~€2). Explore the clifftops and watch surfers at Praia do Tonel below.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sagres village for a sunset drink at a local bar overlooking the Atlantic. Catch the last bus back to Lagos (~18:30 or 19:00 — check timetable). Relax at the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Quick coffee and pastry at Lagos bus station café (~€2)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Nortada in Sagres — fresh grilled fish of the day with salad (~€10-12)
meals.dinner: Self-catering from Pingo Doce supermarket near the hostel — pasta, local cheese, wine (~€5-7)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is very windy — bring a light jacket even on warm days. The last bus from Sagres to Lagos is usually around 19:00-19:30 on weekdays; check the Eva Bus schedule at eva-bus.com. Saturday may have reduced service.

day_by_day.morning: Lazy Sunday morning at the hostel. Visit the Lagos Sunday market (Mercado Municipal) for fresh local produce, olives, almonds, and figs — perfect for snacking. Stock up on budget picnic supplies. Explore the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos, ~€3) — the first slave market in Europe, historically significant.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia do Camilo, a small hidden gem beach accessible via wooden stairs down the cliffs, 10 minutes walk from Ponta da Piedade. It's less crowded on Sunday afternoons. Spend the afternoon swimming and sunbathing in the sheltered cove.
day_by_day.evening: Sunday evening stroll along the Lagos marina. Watch local fishermen and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere. Try a local cervejaria (beer hall) for a cold Super Bock beer (~€1.50) and some petiscos.

meals.breakfast: Market breakfast — fresh fruit, local bread, and a coffee from a market stall (~€3)
meals.lunch: Picnic on Praia do Camilo with market purchases (~€4-5)
meals.dinner: Cervejaria Dois Irmãos or similar — prego no pão (steak sandwich) and beer (~€7-9)

day_by_day.notes: The Slave Market Museum is small but historically important and very affordable. Praia do Camilo has limited space — arrive by early afternoon. The wooden staircase can be slippery when wet.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east to Portimão and Praia da Rocha. Take the Eva Bus from Lagos (~€3.50, 30 minutes). Explore Portimão's waterfront and the Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays, €3 other days) — an excellent museum in a converted sardine canning factory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk south to Praia da Rocha, one of the Algarve's most famous beaches with its wide golden sands and dramatic rock formations. Spend the afternoon swimming and exploring the beach. Walk the cliff-top promenade for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Portimão's riverside dining strip along the Arade River, famous for grilled sardines. This is one of the best and most affordable places in the Algarve for fresh sardines. Return to Lagos by bus (~€3.50).

meals.breakfast: Hostel or local café in Lagos before departure (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia da Rocha — grilled chicken piri-piri wrap (~€5-6)
meals.dinner: Riverside tasca in Portimão — grilled sardines with bread and salad (~€8-10) before catching the bus back

day_by_day.notes: Portimão is very easy to reach from Lagos by bus. The riverside sardine restaurants are a must-try — September is still within sardine season. Check the last bus back to Lagos (usually around 22:00-23:00).

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Take a morning bus or taxi (~€15) to Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (between Lagos and Portimão). This Algarve winery offers affordable tours and tastings (~€10-15 per person). Learn about Algarve wine production and taste regional varieties including Negra Mole and Castelão grapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, visit the nearby town of Silves — take a local bus (~€3). Explore the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry), one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal. Walk the old town and visit the Gothic cathedral (free).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Silves' charming old town at sunset. Return to Lagos by bus (~€3.50). Share wine tasting notes with fellow hostel guests over a bottle of Algarve wine purchased at the winery.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hostel — coffee and tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese, ~€3)
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — light lunch with local wine (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Self-catering at the hostel — charcuterie, local cheese, olives, and winery wine (~€6-8)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Quinta dos Vales winery tour in advance at quintadosvales.eu. Silves is a highlight of the Algarve interior — very different from the coastal towns. The castle views over the Arade valley are spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the western Algarve coast — take a bus or rent a bicycle to Praia do Amado, one of the best surf beaches in Portugal (~30km from Lagos, best reached by car or organized tour). Alternatively, take a surf lesson at Lagos beach with a local surf school (~€25-30 including board and wetsuit).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos and visit the Mercado Municipal for a late lunch. Spend the afternoon at Praia de Porto de Mós, a beautiful and relatively quiet beach 2km south of Lagos center, accessible by a pleasant cliff walk.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free Fado music performance if available at a local restaurant or cultural center in Lagos (check the local tourism office for listings). Alternatively, enjoy the lively bar scene on Rua 25 de Abril.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local padaria (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Mercado Municipal food stalls — fresh grilled fish or bifana (~€5-6)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Galeão in Lagos — affordable set menu with wine (~€10-12)

day_by_day.notes: Check with the Lagos Tourism Office (Posto de Turismo) on Praça Gil Eanes for free cultural events. Surf lessons are a fun budget activity — many schools offer group lessons which are cheaper. Porto de Mós beach has a small beach bar.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Monchique — take a bus from Lagos to Portimão (~€3.50) then connect to Monchique (~€3). Explore this charming mountain town in the Serra de Monchique. Visit the ruins of the Franciscan Convento de Nossa Senhora do Desterro and the town's artisan shops selling medronho (arbutus berry brandy).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike or take a taxi up to Fóia, the highest peak in the Algarve (902m). On a clear day you can see both the Atlantic and the Alentejo plains. The views are spectacular. Sample free medronho tastings at roadside stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Monchique town for dinner before catching the bus back to Portimão and then Lagos. The mountain air is noticeably cooler — bring a light jacket.

meals.breakfast: Quick coffee at Lagos bus station (~€1.50)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central in Monchique — carne de porco à alentejana (pork with clams) or grilled chicken (~€9-11)
meals.dinner: Snack bar in Monchique before the bus — soup and bread (~€4-5)

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is a refreshing change from the coastal heat. The medronho brandy is a local specialty — try before you buy. Bus connections between Monchique and Portimão are infrequent; check the schedule carefully at eva-bus.com to avoid being stranded.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience — visit Adega Cooperativa do Algarve or explore the local wine shops in Lagos for a self-guided tasting. Many wine shops offer free or low-cost tastings of Algarve DOC wines. Alternatively, take a morning bus to Lagoa town (~€4) to visit Adega do Cantor winery (Cliff Richard's famous winery, tours ~€15).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos and spend the afternoon at Praia de Meia Praia — the long, wide beach east of Lagos accessible by ferry (€1.50). This is a great beach for a final relaxed afternoon swim. The beach is 4km long so you can always find a quiet spot.
day_by_day.evening: Friday night in Lagos — the town comes alive. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere on Rua 25 de Abril and the surrounding streets. Have a final special dinner at a slightly nicer restaurant to celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, toast, juice, coffee (~€5)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Meia Praia — grilled chicken and salad (~€7-8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco — seafood cataplana for one with local wine (~€14-16, a slight splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's winery) in Guia near Albufeira is further east but worth it for wine enthusiasts — check if the tour fits your schedule. Friday evenings in Lagos are lively — the hostel bar is a great place to meet fellow travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — head to Praia da Luz one more time or try Praia de Salema, a beautiful fishing village beach 20km west of Lagos (bus ~€3). Salema is quieter than Lagos beaches and has a lovely authentic fishing village atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos by early afternoon. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping — look for local products like Algarve almonds, carob products, local wine, and handmade ceramics at the Mercado Municipal or artisan shops. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening walk through Lagos old town. Visit the Igreja de Santa Maria and the old city walls at sunset for a memorable farewell view. Have a final drink at a rooftop bar or the hostel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a snack bar in Salema village — grilled limpets (lapas) or sardines (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Budget farewell dinner — piri-piri chicken at Frango da Guia or similar (~€8-10) with a glass of Algarve wine

day_by_day.notes: Salema is a hidden gem — much less touristy than Lagos beaches. The fishing boats still come in daily. Buy local almonds and carob products as affordable and authentic souvenirs. Check out time at the hostel — confirm with reception.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Boutique Taghostel (store luggage if needed). Final morning stroll through Lagos — visit the waterfront and the Praça da República one last time. Grab a final pastel de nata and coffee at a local café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, take the Eva Bus or Rede Expressos from Lagos bus station to Faro Airport (~€5-7, 1.5 hours). Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for the journey and check-in. Enjoy the Algarve scenery one last time from the bus window.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the beaches, wines, and culture of the Algarve!

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão (milky coffee) at a Lagos café (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Snack at Faro Airport or pack leftovers from the hostel (~€5-8)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate: Accommodation at Taghostel hostel dorm ~€15-25/night x 12 nights = €180-300. Transport (buses, ferries) ~€50-60 total. Food ~€20-25/day = €260-325. Activities and wine tastings ~€60-80. Total estimated budget: €550-765 for 13 days. Always keep some cash (euros) for small cafés and markets that may not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-booked airport transfer or taxi (~1 hour) to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos. Check in, freshen up, and grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour café or the hostel's common area if available.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at Café Ginginha or a nearby tapas bar open late in Lagos town center – budget €10–15

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid long taxi queues late at night. Confirm check-in arrangements with Taghostel as arrival is after 22:00.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely breakfast, take a short walk to explore Lagos old town – stroll along the historic city walls, visit the Igreja de Santo António, and get oriented with your surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, a long golden beach just 2 km from the hostel (reachable by a short taxi or bike ride). Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing on one of the Algarve's most accessible and beautiful beaches. Rent a sun lounger for €8–10.
day_by_day.evening: Wander back into Lagos town center for dinner. Explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril pedestrian street and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of this charming coastal town.

meals.breakfast: Café Correia on Rua Silva Lopes – classic Portuguese breakfast of pastel de nata, toast, and galão coffee – €5–7
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Meia Praia – grilled sardines, salad, and a cold Sagres beer – €12–16
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant near Lagos – fresh grilled fish and local wine with ocean views – €20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: September is an excellent time to visit – crowds thin out after August but the sea is still warm (around 22°C). Pick up a local SIM card or confirm data roaming for navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim experience. Depart from Lagos by car or organized tour shuttle (~40 min east). Hike the dramatic clifftop trail between Praia da Marinha and Benagil, marveling at golden limestone arches, sea stacks, and hidden coves. The trail is approximately 5 km round trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha beach for a swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters. Explore the small sea caves and rock formations accessible from the beach. Relax on the sand and soak in one of the Algarve's most photogenic settings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed evening in the Taghostel common area, meeting fellow travelers, before heading out for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a packed breakfast from a local padaria (bakery) before departure – croissant, fruit, and coffee – €5
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the beach – pick up local cheese, presunto ham, olives, and bread from a Lagos deli the night before – €8–10
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos – traditional Algarvian cataplana (seafood stew) and local Lagoa wine – €22–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the coastal hike. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. The clifftop paths can be uneven – stay behind safety barriers at all times.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat tour from Lagos Marina departing around 09:30. Explore the famous Ponta da Piedade grottos – a series of stunning sea caves, arches, and golden rock formations just south of Lagos. Tours last approximately 75 minutes and cost €15–20 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia do Camilo, a small secluded beach accessible via a wooden staircase carved into the cliffs, just 10 minutes from the hostel. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing in this intimate cove setting.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely evening in Lagos. Browse the artisan shops and galleries along Rua Cândido dos Reis, then settle in for dinner at a local tasca.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mira Mar near the marina – fresh pastries, fruit juice, and coffee – €6–8
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia do Camilo – prego sandwich (steak roll) and local beer – €10–13
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso in Lagos old town – petiscos (Portuguese tapas) including bacalhau croquettes, grilled octopus, and local wine – €18–24 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ponta da Piedade boat tour in advance, especially on weekends. Arrive at the marina 15 minutes early. Praia do Camilo has limited space – arrive early in the afternoon for the best spots.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour in the Lagoa DOC wine region (~30 km east of Lagos). Depart by organized tour or rental car. Visit the first winery of the day – tour the vineyards, learn about the unique Algarve terroir, and taste local white and rosé wines produced from Arinto and Síria grapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine tour with a second winery visit. Enjoy a guided cellar tour, barrel tasting, and a paired lunch featuring local cheeses, charcuterie, and regional specialties. Learn about the winemaking process unique to the Lagoa DOC appellation.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon. Rest at the hostel before heading out for a relaxed dinner. Consider picking up a bottle of your favorite wine from the tour to enjoy later.

meals.breakfast: Café Central in Lagos – toast with local honey and butter, orange juice, and espresso – €5–7
meals.lunch: Included as part of the vineyard tour – paired wine lunch with regional products – typically included in tour price (€45–65 per person for full tour)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bica in Lagos – grilled sea bream with roasted vegetables and a glass of Algarve wine – €20–26 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour at least 2–3 days in advance. Designate a driver if renting a car, or opt for an organized tour with transport included. September is harvest season – a particularly special time to visit wineries.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow Sunday morning. Sleep in, have a leisurely breakfast, and visit the Lagos Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal) for fresh local produce, fish, and artisan goods – a wonderful window into local daily life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a day trip to Sagres (~30 km west of Lagos by bus or rental car). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress perched on a windswept promontory at the southwestern tip of Europe. Explore the historic wind compass and enjoy breathtaking Atlantic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a sunset walk along the Lagos seafront promenade before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or Café Correia – full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, toast, and coffee – €7–9
meals.lunch: A Sagres – local restaurant in Sagres village – grilled tuna steak with potatoes and salad – €14–18
meals.dinner: No Pátio Restaurant in Lagos – Mediterranean-inspired menu with vegetarian options and local wines – €20–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is windier and cooler than Lagos – bring a light jacket. The last bus back to Lagos typically departs Sagres around 19:00 on Sundays – check the EVA Transportes schedule in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour, departing from Benagil beach (~45 km east of Lagos). Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave – a cathedral-like sea cave with a natural skylight – and explore the surrounding hidden grottos and sea arches along this spectacular coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil or nearby Praia de Carvalho – a hidden gem accessible through a short tunnel in the cliffs. Swim and unwind after the morning's adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Treat yourself to a well-deserved sundowner cocktail at a rooftop bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel or a local café before departure – toast, fruit, and coffee – €5–7
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Benagil beach – fresh fish sandwich and cold drink – €10–13
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos – upscale traditional Portuguese cuisine with excellent local wine list – €28–35 per person (a mid-range splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Kayak Tour well in advance – it is one of the most popular experiences in the Algarve. Wear a swimsuit under your clothes and bring a waterproof bag for your phone and valuables. Tour typically lasts 2–2.5 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or scooter from a Lagos rental shop and explore the coastline at your own pace. Cycle south along the Via Algarviana coastal path toward Praia da Luz (~6 km west), a charming village beach with calm waters and a relaxed atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Praia da Luz. Swim, explore the village, and visit the small Roman ruins museum (Museu Arqueológico) near the beach. Enjoy the quieter pace of this less-touristy coastal village.
day_by_day.evening: Cycle back to Lagos as the sun begins to set. Enjoy the golden hour light over the Atlantic before returning your rental and heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Padaria Portuguesa near the hostel – fresh bread, croissant, and galão – €5
meals.lunch: Fortaleza da Luz restaurant in Praia da Luz – grilled chicken piri-piri with rice and salad – €13–17
meals.dinner: Cervejaria Dois Irmãos in Lagos – seafood platters, cold beer, and a lively local atmosphere – €18–22 per person

day_by_day.notes: Bicycle rental costs approximately €10–15 per day. The coastal road to Praia da Luz is mostly flat and suitable for all fitness levels. Bring a lock for your bike.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Silves (~35 km northeast of Lagos by bus or car). Visit the impressive Castelo de Silves, a well-preserved Moorish castle with panoramic views over the Algarve interior. Explore the charming historic town center and the Gothic cathedral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia in Silves to learn about the region's Moorish heritage. Stroll along the Arade River waterfront and browse the local artisan shops. If visiting on a Wednesday, check for the weekly market.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by late afternoon. Enjoy a quiet evening at the hostel or explore a new neighborhood of Lagos for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagos before departure – pastel de nata and espresso – €4–6
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves – famous for grilled fish and seafood, a local institution – €18–24 per person
meals.dinner: Taberna de Lagos – rustic Portuguese tavern with daily specials, local wine, and a cozy atmosphere – €16–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Buses run regularly between Lagos and Silves (Rede Expressos or EVA). The journey takes approximately 45–60 minutes. Silves castle entrance fee is approximately €3. The town is quieter and more authentic than the coastal resorts.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Lagoa wine region for a self-guided wine exploration. Visit Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's winery) or Quinta dos Vales independently. Take a morning tour of the estate, walk the vineyards, and enjoy a private tasting of their award-winning wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a taxi to the coastal town of Carvoeiro (~35 km east). Explore the picturesque village, walk the Algar Seco boardwalk trail along dramatic rock formations, and swim at the small Praia de Carvoeiro beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a bottle of wine purchased from the morning's winery tasting.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café – €6–8
meals.lunch: Winery restaurant or picnic with wine and local products purchased at the estate – €15–20
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha Velha in Lagos – home-style Portuguese cooking with daily fish specials and local Algarve wine – €18–23 per person

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead to confirm opening hours and tasting availability at your chosen winery. September is harvest season – you may be able to witness the grape harvest in action, a truly special experience.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final morning at Praia de Dona Ana, one of Lagos's most beautiful and iconic beaches, just 2 km from the hostel. Arrive early to secure a good spot. Swim in the calm, sheltered waters framed by dramatic amber cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a stand-up paddleboard (SUP) lesson or rental at Meia Praia beach (~€20–25 per hour). Paddle along the calm bay and enjoy a different perspective of the Lagos coastline. Alternatively, join a dolphin watching boat tour from Lagos Marina (~€35–45 per person, 2 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your penultimate evening in the Algarve with a sunset cocktail at a clifftop bar. Head to the Ponta da Piedade viewpoint for one of the most spectacular sunsets in Portugal.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha in Lagos – full breakfast with eggs, toast, fresh juice, and coffee – €8–10
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Dona Ana – grilled prawns, salad, and a cold drink – €14–18
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vasco da Gama in Lagos – upscale seafood and steak menu with panoramic views – €28–35 per person (farewell splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Book the dolphin watching tour in advance. Common dolphin and bottlenose dolphin sightings are frequent in September. The Ponta da Piedade sunset viewpoint is a 20-minute walk from the hostel – bring a jacket as it can be breezy.

day_by_day.morning: Take a final day trip to Tavira (~120 km east of Lagos, ~1.5 hours by train). This elegant town is considered one of the most beautiful in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, the castle ruins, and the charming whitewashed streets lined with terracotta-roofed churches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira – a stunning barrier island with pristine, unspoiled beaches stretching for kilometers. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing on one of the Algarve's most beautiful and natural beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Enjoy a final evening stroll through Lagos old town, picking up last-minute souvenirs – local wine, fleur de sel, almond sweets, and handmade ceramics.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Lagos train station café before departure – €5–7
meals.lunch: Restaurante Bica in Tavira – fresh clams in garlic and white wine (amêijoas à Bulhão Pato) and grilled fish – €18–24 per person
meals.dinner: O Cantinho do Mar in Lagos – final dinner with a classic cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana) and a bottle of Lagoa DOC wine – €24–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos–Tavira train journey requires a change at Faro. Total journey time is approximately 1.5–2 hours each way. Check CP (Comboios de Portugal) schedules in advance. The ferry to Ilha de Tavira runs frequently and costs approximately €2 each way.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos. Enjoy a slow breakfast and pack your bags. Take one last walk through the historic old town – visit the Mercado Municipal for fresh produce, stop at a local café for a final pastel de nata and espresso, and soak in the atmosphere of this wonderful coastal city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, either relax at the hostel, take a final dip at the nearest beach, or begin your transfer to Faro Airport. Allow at least 1.5 hours travel time from Lagos to Faro Airport plus 2 hours for check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Carry the memories of 13 incredible days in the Algarve – golden cliffs, turquoise waters, sea caves, and exceptional local wines.

meals.breakfast: Final Portuguese breakfast at Café Correia – pastel de nata, toast with local jam, and galão – €6–8
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hostel or a nearby café before departure – soup and sandwich – €8–12
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Faro Airport or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at Taghostel is typically 11:00 – confirm with reception. Ask if you can store luggage until your transfer. Pre-book your airport transfer back to Faro to avoid stress on departure day. Consider purchasing a bottle of Lagoa DOC wine at the airport duty-free as a final souvenir.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim and snorkeling among the rock formations.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local wineries in the Lagoa DOC wine region, the heart of Algarve winemaking. Tour the vineyards, learn about indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco, and enjoy guided tastings of crisp whites, rosés, and robust reds paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most photographed sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos, arched rock formations, and secret beaches along the dramatic Algarve coastline, combining adventure with breathtaking natural beauty.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Local Seafood Dinner
experiences.description: Visit the windswept Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of Europe, for a dramatic Atlantic sunset. Afterward, dine at a traditional tasca in Sagres village, savoring freshly grilled cataplana (seafood stew), percebes (barnacles), and local Algarve wine in an authentic fishing village atmosphere.
experiences.location: Sagres & Cabo de São Vicente, Vila do Bispo

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Oyster Tasting
experiences.description: Take a guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park of tidal channels, barrier islands, and wildlife. Stop at a local oyster farm to taste freshly harvested oysters paired with chilled Algarve white wine, and explore the pristine barrier island beaches accessible only by boat.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer pre-arranged to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (~1 hour drive). Check in, unwind with a welcome glass of local Algarve wine left by the hotel, and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: On flight
meals.lunch: On flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night charcuterie and cheese board arranged by the hotel upon arrival, paired with a glass of Quinta dos Vales white wine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private chauffeur transfer from Faro Airport to Lagos for a seamless luxury arrival. Confirm with hotel for a late check-in and welcome amenity. Keep Day 1 light – rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the hotel, then a gentle orientation walk through the historic old town of Lagos. Explore the 16th-century city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone lanes. Visit the Igreja de Santo António, a stunning baroque church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, a long golden beach just east of Lagos, easily accessible by taxi or hotel shuttle. Rent a premium sun lounger and parasol setup, swim in the calm Atlantic waters, and enjoy the relaxed luxury beach atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos, one of the most celebrated seafood restaurants in the region. Enjoy fresh grilled sea bass, cataplana de marisco (seafood stew), and a bottle of local Algarve white wine on the terrace.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at the hotel – fresh pastries, local cheeses, presunto, fruit, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Light snack and cocktails at the beach bar at Meia Praia – grilled prawns and a chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina – premium seafood tasting menu with local wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery day after travel. Keep the pace slow and indulgent. Meia Praia is only 2 km from the hotel and is ideal for a calm first full beach day.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim: Depart by private car (~30 min east of Lagos) to one of the Algarve's most iconic beaches. Join a guided coastal hike along the dramatic golden limestone cliffs, exploring hidden grottos, sea arches, and panoramic Atlantic viewpoints. Descend to the beach for a refreshing swim in crystal-clear turquoise waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the nearby Praia do Carvalho and Praia de Benagil on foot or by private boat transfer. Enjoy the secluded coves and dramatic cliff scenery. Return to Lagos by private car in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at No Pátio, a refined restaurant in Lagos known for its creative Portuguese cuisine with a modern twist. Try the tuna tataki with algae butter and the slow-roasted Alentejo pork with local wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, artisan breads, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic prepared by the hotel – local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh bread, fruit, and a chilled bottle of rosé enjoyed on the clifftops
meals.dinner: No Pátio Restaurant, Lagos – contemporary Portuguese tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring sunscreen, a hat, and swimwear. The Praia da Marinha hike is moderately easy but involves some uneven terrain. September weather is ideal – warm and sunny with fewer crowds than peak summer.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour: Depart by private car to the Lagoa DOC wine region (~40 min east of Lagos), the heartland of Algarve winemaking. Visit Quinta dos Vales, one of the region's most prestigious estates. Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards, wine cellars, and barrel rooms, learning about the unique terroir of the Algarve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine tour with a visit to a second winery – Adega do Cantor (Sir Cliff Richard's celebrated estate) or Quinta da Penina. Enjoy a premium guided tasting of 6–8 wines including the region's signature Negra Mole reds and crisp Arinto whites, paired with local artisan cheeses and charcuterie.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Dinner at Casinha do Petisco, a beloved local gem known for its authentic Algarvian cuisine. Enjoy petiscos (Portuguese tapas) including percebes (barnacles), amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams), and grilled octopus.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – full spread with fresh pastries, yogurt, local honey, and espresso
meals.lunch: Wine and food pairing lunch at the vineyard – artisan cheeses, presunto, olives, fresh bread, and estate wines
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco, Lagos – authentic Algarvian petiscos with a curated local wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the vineyard tour in advance and arrange a private driver for the day – wine tasting and driving do not mix. Quinta dos Vales also offers a sculpture garden and art installations, making it a culturally rich experience beyond just wine.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour: Depart by private car to Praia de Benagil (~30 min east of Lagos). Join a premium small-group or private kayak tour to paddle through the world-famous Benagil Cave – a cathedral-like sea cave with a natural skylight opening. Explore hidden sea caves, arches, and grottos along the dramatic coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil or nearby Praia de Carvalho. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon swimming and sunbathing on these stunning secluded beaches. Return to Lagos by private car in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the rooftop bar of a Lagos hotel or at Ponta da Piedade viewpoint, watching the golden light illuminate the iconic rock formations. Dinner at Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro, ~25 min), a Michelin-starred restaurant offering an extraordinary tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – smoothie bowls, avocado toast, local pastries, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at Restaurante O Litoral in Carvoeiro – grilled fresh fish, seafood rice, and chilled local white wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon, Carvoeiro – Michelin-starred tasting menu with full wine pairing (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil kayak tour early in the morning to avoid afternoon winds and crowds. A private tour is highly recommended for a premium experience. Bon Bon requires advance reservation – book weeks ahead as it is one of the Algarve's most sought-after dining experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning in Lagos. Visit the Mercado Municipal de Lagos (local market) for fresh produce, local cheeses, honey, and artisan goods. Stroll along the marina and enjoy a slow espresso at a waterfront café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat charter from Lagos Marina for an exclusive afternoon along the Ponta da Piedade coastline. Explore the golden sea stacks, hidden grottos, and sea caves by private boat. Swim in secluded coves accessible only by water. Enjoy chilled champagne and canapés on board.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Villas Alvor Boutique Hotel's restaurant or at Restaurante Quatro Águas in Tavira (if willing to travel). Alternatively, enjoy a premium dinner at Restaurante Laranjeira in Lagos – a sophisticated spot with an excellent wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Café Paraíso, Lagos – one of the oldest and most charming cafés in the city, serving traditional pastéis de nata, toasted sandwiches, and galão coffee
meals.lunch: Champagne, chilled rosé, fresh fruit, and gourmet canapés served on the private boat charter
meals.dinner: Restaurante Laranjeira, Lagos – refined Portuguese cuisine with an extensive wine list in an elegant setting

day_by_day.notes: Private boat charters from Lagos Marina can be arranged for 3–4 hours and typically include a skipper, snorkeling equipment, and onboard refreshments. This is one of the most memorable experiences in the Algarve and ideal for a luxury trip.

day_by_day.morning: Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Day Trip: Depart by private car to Sagres (~30 min west of Lagos). Visit the imposing Fortaleza de Sagres, the historic fortress from which Portuguese explorers launched their Age of Discovery voyages. Explore the windswept promontory and the giant wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Cabo de São Vicente – the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Stand at the edge of the world where the Atlantic stretches endlessly. Explore the dramatic 60-meter cliffs and the historic lighthouse. Browse the artisan market stalls for local crafts and smoked fish.
day_by_day.evening: Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Local Seafood Dinner: Watch the legendary sunset at Cabo de São Vicente, one of the most dramatic sunsets in Europe as the sun dips into the Atlantic. Dinner at Restaurante Memmo Baleeira in Sagres – a premium restaurant with panoramic ocean views, serving the freshest local seafood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – full Portuguese spread with local honey, fresh fruit, and artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Restaurante A Sagres in Sagres village – grilled fresh fish, percebes, and local wine with ocean views
meals.dinner: Restaurante Memmo Baleeira, Sagres – premium seafood dinner with sunset views, featuring local lobster, grilled turbot, and Algarve wines

day_by_day.notes: Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente can be windy even in September – bring a light jacket. The sunset at Cabo de São Vicente is legendary and should not be missed. Arrive at least 30 minutes before sunset to secure a prime viewing spot on the cliffs.

day_by_day.morning: Spa and wellness morning at the hotel or at a nearby luxury spa. Book a 90-minute treatment – consider a traditional Portuguese hot stone massage or an Algarve sea salt scrub. Spend the remaining morning relaxing by the pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia do Camilo, one of the most beautiful and intimate beaches near Lagos, accessible via a wooden staircase carved into the golden cliffs. Enjoy a premium beach setup with sun loungers, and swim in the sheltered turquoise cove.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo at Ponta da Piedade viewpoint, then dinner at Restaurante Atlântico at the Cascade Wellness Resort in Lagos – a sophisticated fine dining experience with panoramic Atlantic views and an exceptional wine list.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast service – fresh fruit platter, smoked salmon, scrambled eggs, artisan breads, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach café near Praia do Camilo – grilled sardines, salad, and a chilled glass of Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Restaurante Atlântico, Cascade Wellness Resort, Lagos – fine dining tasting menu with Atlantic views and premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Camilo is a short taxi ride or 20-minute walk from the hotel. It is one of the most photogenic beaches in the Algarve. Book the spa treatment in advance. The Cascade Resort restaurant is one of the finest dining venues in Lagos.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves – the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve (~45 min from Lagos by private car). Visit the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves, one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal. Explore the medieval cathedral and the charming old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local orange grove or almond farm near Silves for a private tasting experience of fresh Algarve citrus, local honey, and medronho (arbutus berry brandy). Alternatively, visit Quinta da Figueirinha winery near Silves for an intimate wine tasting in a beautiful rural setting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Dinner at Restaurante Dom Sebastião, one of Lagos's most iconic and long-standing fine dining restaurants, known for its exceptional cataplana dishes and extensive Portuguese wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – eggs any style, local cheeses, fresh pastries, and espresso
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves – a legendary seafood restaurant famous for its grilled fish and seafood rice, beloved by locals and food critics alike
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião, Lagos – traditional Algarvian fine dining with cataplana specialties and a world-class wine list

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a hidden gem often overlooked by tourists. The castle offers stunning views over the orange groves and the Arade River valley. September is harvest season in the Algarve, making farm and vineyard visits particularly special.

day_by_day.morning: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Oyster Tasting: Depart early by private car to Faro (~1 hour east of Lagos). Join a premium guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system – a UNESCO-protected natural park of tidal channels, barrier islands, and salt marshes. Spot flamingos, herons, and other migratory birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Ria Formosa experience with a stop at a traditional oyster farm for a premium oyster tasting directly from the water. Enjoy freshly harvested oysters with lemon and local white wine on the boat. Explore the barrier island of Ilha Deserta – a pristine, car-free island with crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by private car. Dinner at Restaurante Faz Gostos in Lagos – a charming restaurant in a historic building known for its creative Portuguese cuisine and excellent wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast – light and energizing with fresh fruit, yogurt, granola, and coffee before the drive to Faro
meals.lunch: Freshly harvested oysters, local cheeses, crusty bread, and chilled Alvarinho white wine enjoyed on the boat in Ria Formosa
meals.dinner: Restaurante Faz Gostos, Lagos – creative Portuguese cuisine with local ingredients and a curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Ria Formosa tour is a full-day excursion. Book a private or small-group premium tour for the best experience. Bring binoculars for birdwatching – September is an excellent time for migratory bird species. The oyster tasting on the water is an unmissable luxury highlight.

day_by_day.morning: Second Algarve Wine Experience: Return to the Lagoa wine region for a deeper dive into Algarve wines. Visit Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa, the oldest wine cooperative in the Algarve, for a guided cellar tour and tasting of their premium reserve wines. Learn about the unique microclimate and indigenous grape varieties of the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming town of Lagoa and nearby Carvoeiro village. Stroll along the Carvoeiro boardwalk, admire the dramatic cliff scenery, and browse local boutiques. Relax at Praia de Carvoeiro for a late afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a farewell-style premium dinner at Restaurante Bon Bon (if not visited on Day 5) or at Restaurante Vasco da Gama in Lagos – a sophisticated waterfront restaurant with exceptional seafood and an impressive wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – full spread with smoked salmon, local cheeses, fresh pastries, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro – fresh seafood with panoramic cliff views and local wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vasco da Gama, Lagos Marina – premium waterfront dining with fresh lobster, grilled turbot, and an extensive Portuguese wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Lagoa wine cooperative offers some of the best value premium wines in the Algarve and is an excellent place to purchase bottles to take home. Carvoeiro is one of the most picturesque villages in the Algarve and worth a leisurely afternoon exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning at Praia Dona Ana, one of the most beautiful and iconic beaches near Lagos, just a short walk or taxi ride from the hotel. Enjoy a premium sun lounger setup, swim in the sheltered golden cove, and soak in the stunning cliff scenery one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a final afternoon of leisure. Visit the Museu de Lagos for a fascinating insight into the city's history from prehistoric times through the Age of Discovery. Browse the boutique shops along Rua 25 de Abril for artisan gifts, local ceramics, and Portuguese wine to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the finest restaurant of the trip. Return to Restaurante Bon Bon (Michelin-starred, Carvoeiro) for the ultimate culinary send-off, or enjoy a private chef dinner experience arranged through the hotel for an intimate in-house farewell.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast – full premium spread with champagne mimosas to celebrate the final full day
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Camilo, Lagos – a legendary cliffside restaurant perched above Praia do Camilo, serving exceptional grilled fish and seafood with breathtaking views
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred farewell dinner at Restaurante Bon Bon, Carvoeiro – the ultimate luxury dining experience in the Algarve with full tasting menu and wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Praia Dona Ana is walkable from the hotel (approximately 15 minutes). Pack any wine purchases carefully for the flight home. Consider purchasing a bottle of Quinta dos Vales Grande Reserva or Adega do Cantor as a premium souvenir. Confirm checkout time with the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos. Enjoy a last slow breakfast at the hotel. Take a final stroll along the Lagos waterfront promenade and say goodbye to the Atlantic. Check out of the hotel and arrange private luxury transfer to Faro Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Lagos by private chauffeur to Faro Airport (~1 hour). Allow ample time for check-in and security. Enjoy the airport lounges before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days in the Algarve – golden cliffs, turquoise waters, world-class wines, and unforgettable seafood.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast – a leisurely and indulgent spread to close out the trip in style
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a quick stop at a café in Lagos before departure
meals.dinner: On flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight departure for the transfer and airport procedures. Pre-arrange the private transfer the evening before. Consider purchasing last-minute local products at the airport – Algarve wines, local honey, and carob products make excellent gifts.

query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September from London
